title: January 2026 Protests: Hossein Darabi Sentenced to 25 Years in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Hossein Darabi, one of the detainees arrested during the January 2026 protests, has been sentenced to 25 years in prison.

Based on information received by HRANA, the sentence was issued by Branch 28 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court on the charge of “collaboration with hostile governments.”

A source close to Darabi’s family confirmed the news to HRANA, stating: “Hossein Darabi was notified of his 25-year prison sentence on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, while held in Greater Tehran Prison.”

Darabi was previously arrested during the January 2026 protests and remains incarcerated in Greater Tehran Prison.
snippet: According to HRANA, Hossein Darabi, one of the detainees arrested during the January 2026 protests, has been sentenced to 25 years in prison.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Mohammad Aref Shahbakhsh Executed
content:
According to HRANA, citing Mizan News Agency, Mohammad Aref Shahbakhsh was executed at dawn today, November 7, 2026.

The Judiciary’s Media Center claimed that Shahbakhsh had ties to the Jaish al-Adl group and was identified and arrested as one of the main suspects in an armed attack on the Qaleh Bid police outpost in Khash County, which resulted in several law enforcement officers being killed or injured.

The case was initially opened at Branch 3 of the Investigation Department of the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor’s Office in Iranshahr and was subsequently referred to Branch 6 of the Investigation Department of the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor’s Office in Zahedan for further proceedings.

According to the report, Shahbakhsh was ultimately sentenced to death on charges of baghi (armed rebellion) and moharebeh (enmity against God) for his alleged participation in the armed attack on the Qaleh Bid police outpost in Khash County. The sentence was carried out on November 7, 2026.

The report did not specify the location of the execution, the date of Shahbakhsh’s arrest, or any details regarding his access to legal counsel and the judicial proceedings in his case.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Mizan News Agency, Mohammad Aref Shahbakhsh was executed at dawn today, November 7, 2026.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Several Citizens Arrested by Security Forces in Qasr-e Qand
content:
According to HRANA, citing Rasank, a group of residents of Qasr-e Qand have been arrested.

According to the report, security forces arrived in several vehicles at the villages of Kand, Chandukan, and Pask on the morning of Friday, November 6, and arrested several residents of these villages.

The report did not provide further details, including the number or identities of those arrested.

At the time of this report, no information was available regarding the agency responsible for the arrests, the specific allegations, the detainees’ whereabouts, or the charges brought against them.

It should be noted that the villages of Kand, Chandukan, and Pask are located in Qasr-e Qand County, Sistan and Baluchestan Province.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Rasank, a group of residents of Qasr-e Qand have been arrested.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: January 2026 Protests: Hamid Kazemi and Hassan Divand Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, the Revolutionary Court has sentenced Hamid Kazemi and Hassan Divand, two protesters held in Karaj Central Prison, to death.

Based on information obtained by HRANA, the two men were sentenced to death by Branch 2 of the Karaj Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Sabzevari, in a case related to the January 2026 protests. The sentences were issued on the charge of “operational action,” with the court citing provisions concerning the intensification of punishments under the Islamic Penal Code.

Hamid Kazemi and Hassan Divand were arrested by security forces during the nationwide protests last winter and subsequently transferred to Karaj Central Prison.

HRANA’s investigation into the specific allegations against the two men and the latest developments in their legal cases remains ongoing.

Background of the January 2026 Protests

title: Mahmoud Pileh Arrested by Security Forces in Miandoab
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, Mahmoud Pileh, a resident of Gugajlu village in Miandoab County, has been arrested.

According to the report, Pileh was arrested by security agents in Miandoab on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, without the presentation of a judicial warrant.

At the time of this report, no information was available regarding the reasons for his arrest, his place of detention, or the charges brought against him.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, Mahmoud Pileh, a resident of Gugajlu village in Miandoab County, has been arrested.

title: Ali Doraghi Arrested by Security Forces in Ahvaz
content:
According to HRANA, citing Moj Ahvaz, Ali Doraghi (Abdolal Doraghi), 60, was arrested in Ahvaz on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

According to information obtained by HRANA, Doraghi had been summoned to the Ministry of Intelligence’s Information Office through a telephone call and a judicial summons prior to his arrest. However, he was unable to appear due to a heart condition and a history of cardiac surgery. Ultimately, on Tuesday, Ministry of Intelligence agents went to his residence and arrested him.

Doraghi’s medical condition has raised concerns among his family and relatives regarding his health and access to medical care during detention.

No information has been obtained regarding the reasons for his arrest, the charges against him, his place of detention, or his access to legal counsel and medical services.

Ali Doraghi, 60, a resident of Ahvaz, has previously faced legal proceedings and arrest in connection with his activities.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Moj Ahvaz, Ali Doraghi (Abdolal Doraghi), 60, was arrested in Ahvaz on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Motaleb Ahmadian’s Health Deteriorates Amid Denial of Medical Furlough in His 16th Year of Imprisonment
content:
According to HRANA, Motaleb Ahmadian, a political prisoner held in Evin Prison, is suffering from poor physical health and faces serious obstacles to receiving medical treatment due to cancer and its associated complications.

According to information obtained by HRANA, Ahmadian has undergone several surgeries due to complications arising from a cancerous tumor. During these procedures, his gallbladder was removed, and portions of his liver and intestines were also operated on. The repeated surgeries and resulting damage to his digestive system have made further surgical intervention extremely risky.

During his most recent consultation with specialist physicians and surgeons, Ahmadian was informed, following an assessment of his condition, that further surgery was no longer possible. However, according to information received, his physical condition requires an urgent surgical procedure. The surgery currently needed is not directly related to the original operation to remove the cancerous tumor but has become necessary due to complications resulting from that procedure.

title: January 2026 Protests: Amir Delshad Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Amir Delshad, one of those arrested during the January 2026 protests, has been sentenced to death.

Based on information received by HRANA, Branch 5 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Hossein Yazdankhah, with Seyed Reza Javad Mousavi serving as an advisory judge, sentenced Delshad to death on charges including carrying out operations detrimental to national security and interests on behalf of an opposition group through active participation in the January 2026 protests, as well as setting fire to and destroying public property.

An informed source told HRANA regarding the latest developments in Delshad’s case: “Amir Delshad’s appeal has been registered with the Supreme Court.”

Amir Delshad was arrested by security forces during the January 2026 protests and is currently held in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad.

Background of the January 2026 Protests
snippet: According to HRANA, Amir Delshad, one of those arrested during the January 2026 protests, has been sentenced to death.

title: January Protests: Matin Shabani Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Matin Shabani has been sentenced to death. The sentence was issued by Branch 5 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Hossein Yazdankhah, with Seyed Reza Javad Mousavi serving as an advisory judge. The verdict, which was communicated to Mr. Shabani in prison some time ago, sentenced him to death on charges including moharebeh (enmity against God) through participation in the destruction of public property and setting fire to religious centers, as well as assembly and collusion against the country.

A source familiar with the case confirmed the news to HRANA, stating: “During the protests on January 8 and 9, 2026, in Shandiz, a mosque and a Dar al-Quran (Quranic education center) caught fire, and a case was opened in connection with these incidents.”

Matin Shabani was arrested in Shandiz during the nationwide January protests, along with six other citizens who were detained separately. After some time, he was transferred to Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad.

title: Four Citizens Arrested, Several Others Summoned Over Publication of Religious Content
content:
According to HRANA, citing Mizan News Agency, the Judiciary’s Media Center announced that a judicial case had been opened in connection with religious activities on social media and that four citizens had been arrested in this regard.

According to the report, four members of a group known as “Asma Academy” have been formally charged with “promotional activities contrary to the sacred laws of Islam through making baseless and false claims in religious matters,” and detention orders have been issued against them. Several other individuals affiliated with the group have also been summoned by judicial authorities for questioning.

The Judiciary’s Media Center claimed that members of the group, in collaboration with several social media activists and with the aim of generating income, had produced and published religious content, created podcasts, offered educational courses and packages, and organized both in-person and online seminars and workshops.
